title: Your day, separable verbs and dates

items.explanation: Review (Unit 1): in a W-question the question word comes first, then the verb.

items.question: Which article goes with Wohnung?
items.explanation: Review (Unit 2): nouns ending in -ung are always die: die Wohnung.

items.instruction: Fill in the gaps: I get up at half past six.
items.explanation: aufstehen splits: stehe in second place, auf at the very end. halb sieben = 6:30.

answers: Der Kurs fängt um neun an
Um neun fängt der Kurs an
items.explanation: anfangen splits: fängt in second place, an at the end. fängt has an ä with er/sie/es.

items.question: Which sentence means 'Are you coming along?'
items.explanation: mitkommen: in a yes/no question the verb comes first, and mit still goes to the end.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: First I have breakfast, then I work.
items.explanation: zuerst = first; it takes position 1, so the verb follows: Zuerst frühstücke ich.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: Today is the first of May.
items.explanation: 1st is irregular: erste. After der: der erste Mai.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: My birthday is on the seventh of July.
items.explanation: 7th is irregular: siebte. After am the ending is -ten: am siebten Juli.

items.question: When is the birthday?
items.explanation: Juni and Juli sound alike: listen for the n or the l. That's why people say Juno and Julei on the phone.

items.text: Im Winter ist es früh dunkel.
items.explanation: im + season: im Winter. früh = early, with ü.

items.question: Your colleague has a birthday today. What do you say?
items.explanation: Alles Gute zum Geburtstag! = Happy birthday! On the day itself, not before.

items.instruction: Write 4-5 sentences: when your birthday is, and what you do on a Saturday and when (get up, shopping, evening). Use at least two separable verbs (aufstehen, einkaufen, fernsehen ...). Claude will check it.
items.prompt: Wann hast du Geburtstag? Was machst du am Samstag?
